title: Crossed effects of audio-visual environment on indoor soundscape perception for pleasant open-plan office environments
research_question: To investigate the crossed effects of audio-visual physical parameters on the perceived affective quality and overall quality of an OPO environment, and to determine the crossed effects of audio-visual attributes on the overall quality of an OPO environment to propose a strategy for improving work satisfaction and productivity.

participants.description: 34 university students (25 males, 9 females) aged 20-33 years (mean 24.85, SD 3.56) from South Korea, with experience working in an office space.
participants.recruitment: Enlisted based on experience of working in an office space.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: 24 audio-visual stimuli: 3 audio conditions (low, middle, high Lp,A,S,4m) combined with 8 visual conditions (4 OPO layouts x 2 window views). Visual layouts varied in window area ratio (10-45%), W/L (1.00-1.97), floor area (57-585 m²), and floor area per person (10.6-24.2 m²). Window views were 'good' (pleasant urban space) or 'bad' (underdeveloped urban space). Audio stimuli were 1-min male speech samples convoluted with room impulse responses and mixed with 47 dB LAeq background noise.

mechanisms: The relationship between work satisfaction and task performance must be considered for a balanced OPO design.
Creating a visually bright, spacious, and well-organized space with a dry, acoustically calm environment having minimal reverberation is highly effective in improving the overall quality of the OPO.
implementation_implications: To improve overall sound quality, it is desirable to provide an office soundscape with a lower Lp,A,S,4m value (below 48 dB) and higher D2,s (higher than 7 dB).
Designing a bright, wide, and organized indoor space is vital for visual satisfaction and visual privacy, achievable by providing good window views.
If office location cannot be changed, increasing openness by enlarging windows or maintaining a low number of occupants can be beneficial.
Improving visual design can positively affect the perception of noise and variations in the acoustic aspect, thus visual methods should be actively used.
When designing a workspace, a visual environment design must balance work satisfaction and task performance based on client needs.

limitations: Only subjects in their 20s participated, limiting generalizability.
Normality was not achieved in statistical tests.
Only visual and audio stimuli in a limited office space were used, limiting the possibility of obtaining a clear cognitive model.
Lack of gender balance in recruited subjects.
Task performance quantified only with digit span test, not various cognitive skills used in actual tasks.
Short-term stimuli used, not considering long-term effects (fatigue, stress).
Audio-visual attributes selected through a small focus group interview, not representing the general OPO soundscape.
Limited to visual and auditory senses, not considering other indoor environmental quality factors (air, thermal, etc.).
Only male sound sources were used, not considering female voices with different fundamental frequencies.
Further research needed to determine effects of individual worker characteristics (sensitivity, work satisfaction, career, gender, education, economic level).
